author: Shares Investment
title: Apple Shock Negative Earnings Guidance Shook Up Hi-P’s Stock Price
text:
On 3 January 2019, US major smartphone maker Apple revised its earnings forecasts:
Revenue of approximately $84 billion Gross margin of approximately 38 percent Operating expenses of approximately $8.7 billion Other income/(expense) of approximately $550 million Tax rate of approximately 16.5 percent before discrete items According to earnings estimates provided on Yahoo! Finance website, the average revenue and earnings per share (EPS) estimates for the December 2018 quarter were US$91.5 billion and US$4.65 per share respectively.
For the 2019 estimates, the current revenue and EPS consensus are US$277.91 billion, and US$13.29 per share. The revenue estimates for 2019 were in the range between US$269 billion to US$292.33 billion, while the EPS estimate for 2019 a month ago was approximately US$13.38 per share.
The downgrade in AAPL’s December 2018 quarter earnings guidance took down the share price from the closing price of US$157.92 on 02 January 2019 to US$142.19 at the market close on 03 January.
A Negative Bout For Hi-P International
Hi-P International (Hi-P) is one of the major suppliers for Apple’s. According to the AppleInsider.com , Hi-P was an existing supplier of the plastic chassis. However, there were no official disclosures of the estimates of the supply and earnings exposures of Hi-P’s commercial relationship with AAPL.
Hi-P Share Price After AAPL’s Announcement
Hi-P More How will Hi-P be impacted by the latest AAPL earnings forecast downgrade?
At a market capitalisation of S$688.58 million and share price of S$0.86 as of 04 January 2019 based on data provided by Yahoo! Finance, Hi-P’s trailing twelve months (TTM) earnings per share (EPS) is about 6.0 times, and price-to-book (P/B) multiple is 1.3 times.
Source: Phillip Securities Pte Ltd (04 January 2019)
During the nine months ending 30 September 2018 quarter, the Company’s total revenue was $960.22 million, an increase of 2.7 percent from 2017 year-to-date (YTD) revenue of $935.05 million. The earnings attributable to shareholders were $56.17 million or 6.94 Singapore cents in earnings per share for the nine months. This was a 9.2 percent decline the previous year.
hi-p2 More Source: Company’s Financial Statements
The Company’s cash and cash equivalents as at 30 September 2018 stood at $234.5 million, with interest bearing debt comprising notes payable, and short-term borrowings amounting to $174 million (Notes Payable of $822,000 and Short-Term Borrowings of $173.2 million). The Company has positive net operating cash flows (Net OCF) of $90.3 million as of the nine months period ending 30 September 2018. However, this was down from the Net OCF of $192.8 million during the similar period last year in 2017.
According to estimates provided by Yahoo! Finance, the Company’s total debt-to-equity ratio for the most recent quarter (mrq ending 30 September 2018) was 32.9 times, and current ratio was at 1.3 times. Like AAPL, Hi-P also issued a set of mixed to negative earnings guidance for FY18:
The Group expects lower revenue and profit for 4Q18 as compared to 4Q17. The Group expects higher revenue and profit for 2H18 as compared to 1H18. The Group expects lower revenue and profit for FY18 as compared to FY17. What Next For Hi-P Shareholders
On 03 January 2019, the Company bought back 325,700 shares for a total consideration of $281.789.50. This is equivalent of a 1.115 percent of the Company’s cumulative share count of 9,017,500 shares. On 11 January, the company bought another 263,300 shares for a total consideration of $237,111.79.0 Hi-P may have undertook the share buyback transaction in response to the undervaluation of the share price which about 6 times trailing-12months earnings following the negative impacts from AAPL’s latest earnings forecast downgrade.
